mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% over three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a single month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a single month, it signals a robust recovery in the labor market, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate over three months signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and increases investment in equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the easing cycle is identified.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures increase by more than 1% in a single quarter and the consumer price index also increases by more than 0.5% in the same period, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with strong consumer demand, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to potential monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 2% in a single month signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
